_doc: The Literature Links text layer, one definition: the rule $WIKILEAN's site/anchor_resolve.py states in its module docstring and implements as text_layer.
Every case is a synthetic MediaWiki-shaped body; 'layer' is what that function gave for 'html', run from the module whose commit and sha256 are under 'producer'.

formal-companion's renderer (scripts/sources/render_html.py) must give 'layer' on every case without 'known_divergence'. A known divergence is where the two differ: 'departs' names the side that is not the HTML5 parser there ($WIKILEAN's scanner, this renderer, or both), its reason says why, and 'formal_companion_layer' is the layer this repository gives there.
Generated by tests/gen_text_layer.py; replayed by tests/test_locate_text_layer.py. Regenerate it from a newer commit with `python3 tests/gen_text_layer.py --wikilean <checkout>`.

cases.html:
Made-up notion in widget theory
Not to be confused with Gadget.

In widget theory, a flange of a widget W{\displaystyle W} is a subset closed under the widget operation.[1] The flange of order n is written Fn.

Definition

[edit]

Let W{\displaystyle W} be a widget. Then:

F=W{\displaystyle F=W}
Flange theorem — Every finite widget W{\displaystyle W} has a flange.

References

[edit]
  1. ^ Example, A. (2001). Widgets. Synthetic Press. p. 12.

cases.name: pre-leading-newline
cases.why: a pre whose content starts with a newline
cases.html:
Example:

x = 1

known_divergence.reason: the HTML5 tree builder drops one newline right after a pre start tag, so the layer is 'Example:x = 1'; $WIKILEAN's scanner keeps it as White_Space, giving 'Example: x = 1'; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: reference-without-semicolon
cases.why: character references with no ';'
cases.html: R& D and ©2016 and order n.

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 decodes '&amp', '&copy' and '&#160' with no ';' (a parse error, still decoded); $WIKILEAN's scanner decodes only '&...;' and keeps the rest as text; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: reference-longer-than-16
cases.why: a named reference longer than sixteen characters
cases.html: ∳ x

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 knows every named reference; $WIKILEAN's scanner looks for the ';' within sixteen characters of the '&' and keeps a longer one as text; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: abrupt-comments
cases.why: the comments '<!-->' and '<!-- --!>'
cases.html: ABC

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 closes '<!-->' at once and a comment at '--!>'; $WIKILEAN's scanner closes a comment only at a '-->' after its '<!--', so it reads the rest of the page as one comment; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: abrupt-comment-dash
cases.why: the empty comment '<!--->'
cases.html: ab-->c

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 closes '<!--->' at once (an abrupt closing of an empty comment), so 'b-->c' is text; $WIKILEAN's scanner closes a comment only at a '-->' after its '<!--', the one after 'b'; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: gt-in-quoted-attribute
cases.why: a '>' inside a quoted attribute value
cases.html: x y

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 reads a quoted attribute value to its closing quote; $WIKILEAN's scanner ends a tag at its first '>', so the rest of the value becomes text; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: comment-in-attribute
cases.why: a '<!-- -->' inside a quoted attribute value
cases.html: a b

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 reads the attribute value as a value; $WIKILEAN's scanner ends the tag at the '>' of the '-->' inside it; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: cdata-in-html
cases.why: a CDATA section in HTML content
cases.html: ab

known_divergence.reason: in HTML content HTML5 reads '<![CDATA[x]]>' as a bogus comment, no text; $WIKILEAN's scanner keeps it as text; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: markup-declarations
cases.why: a doctype, a declaration and a processing instruction in the body
cases.html: abcd

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 reads each as a doctype or bogus comment, no text; $WIKILEAN's scanner keeps them as text; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: bogus-end-tags
cases.why: the end tags '</>' and '</ x>'
cases.html: abc

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 ignores '</>' and reads '</ x>' as a bogus comment; $WIKILEAN's scanner keeps both as text; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: rcdata-and-rawtext
cases.why: markup inside textarea, title and xmp
cases.html:
ab&<i>u</i>c

<b>x</b>d

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 reads the content of textarea and title as text with references decoded, and that of xmp as raw text, so the markup inside is text; $WIKILEAN's scanner reads it as tags; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: skipped-end-tag-prefix
cases.why: '</styles>' inside a style, '</templates>' inside a template
cases.html: acf

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 ends a style's raw text only at '</style' followed by whitespace, '/' or '>', and '</templates>' is the end tag of another element, ignored, so 'b' and 'e' are skipped content and the layer is 'acf'; $WIKILEAN's scanner ends a skipped element at the first '</style' or '</template' even as the prefix of a longer name, giving 'abcef'; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: skipped-name-prefix
cases.why: a start tag whose name only begins with 'style'
cases.html: abc

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 reads a tag name up to whitespace, '/' or '>', so '<style.x>' is an unknown element whose text counts ('abc'); $WIKILEAN's scanner reads a tag name as [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9:-]*, 'style', and skips to the next '</style' ('ac'); this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: nested-template
cases.why: a template inside a template
cases.html: Ad

known_divergence.reason: in HTML5 everything inside the outer template is its content, so the layer is 'Ad'; $WIKILEAN's scanner skips to the first '</template' and keeps 'c'; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: cdata-in-mathml
cases.why: a CDATA section inside MathML
cases.html: xy

known_divergence.reason: here NEITHER follows HTML5, which makes a CDATA section in foreign content text ('xy'): $WIKILEAN's scanner keeps the markup as text, and html.parser reads every CDATA section as a declaration, which this renderer drops ('y'); MediaWiki's math output holds no CDATA

cases.name: svg-self-closing-style
cases.why: a self-closing style inside SVG
cases.html: alpha gamma words here

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 honours the self-closing flag on an SVG element, so '<style/>' is an empty SVG style and 'beta' is text ('alpha beta gamma words here'); $WIKILEAN's scanner reads it as a style start tag and skips to the next '</style', of which there is none, so nothing after it is text ('alpha'); MediaWiki's math output holds no self-closing style or script; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: mathml-self-closing-script
cases.why: a self-closing script inside MathML
cases.html: alpha xy gamma

known_divergence.reason: HTML5 honours the self-closing flag on a MathML element, so '<script/>' is empty and 'y' and ' gamma' are text ('alpha xy gamma'); $WIKILEAN's scanner reads it as a script start tag and skips to the next '</script', of which there is none ('alpha x'); MediaWiki's math output holds no self-closing style or script; this renderer follows the HTML5 tokenizer

cases.name: template-in-list-item
cases.why: an li start tag inside a template closes no list item outside it
cases.html: • ac

known_divergence.reason: the li start tag inside the template closes the li outside it, and the template with it, so 'b' and 'c' are text here ('abc'); HTML5 and $WIKILEAN give 'ac'; MediaWiki's parser output carries no <template> element, so no page reaches this, and following HTML5 here moves layers: a new renderer id, never an edit of this one

cases.name: template-in-definition-list
cases.why: a dd start tag inside a template closes no dd outside it
cases.html: ac

known_divergence.reason: the dd start tag inside the template closes the dd outside it, and the template with it ('abc'); HTML5 and $WIKILEAN give 'ac'; MediaWiki's parser output carries no <template> element, so no page reaches this, and following HTML5 here moves layers: a new renderer id, never an edit of this one

cases.name: template-in-table-cell
cases.why: td and tr start tags inside a template close no cell or row outside it

known_divergence.reason: the td and tr start tags inside the templates close the cell and the row outside them, and the templates with them ('abcdef'); HTML5 and $WIKILEAN give 'acdf'; MediaWiki's parser output carries no <template> element, so no page reaches this, and following HTML5 here moves layers: a new renderer id, never an edit of this one
